description: 6 exemplars (one German) + 3 near-misses + 2 counterexamples. Authored 2026-10-13 under road-to-skill-scripts-that-run-where-they-land, which rewrote this skill's grounded-corpus invocation to the bundled `node <skills-root>/…/ground.mjs` form and so brought it into check_routing_coverage's touched-skill scope. Exemplars cover the four surfaces its own description names — a query written by hand, a raw statement inside a migration, a seeder bulk-insert, and the parameterization defect — plus the symptom-first phrasing the description singles out: a pasted query and the question why it is slow. Near-misses are three neighbours that share database vocabulary and are somebody else's job: expressing the same read through the ORM (eloquent), deciding the shape of the tables (database), and the index/migration decision behind a slow query (database again, from the other side). Counterexamples guard the letters SQL: a licensing question and a training-deck section both say SQL and ask for no query.

queries.q: why is this slow? SELECT * FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.id WHERE o.created_at > ?
write the raw SQL for the monthly revenue report — the query builder cannot express this window function
this DB::select drops $email straight into the string — fix it
the migration needs a DB::statement for the generated column — write it
write a seeder that bulk-inserts 50k demo rows with raw SQL instead of 50k model saves
warum ist diese Query so langsam? SELECT * FROM orders JOIN order_items ON ...
rewrite this join as an Eloquent relationship with eager loading
queries.note: same read, through the ORM → eloquent

queries.q: should orders and invoices be one table or two?
which index would make this filter fast, and how do I add it?
queries.note: shares the slow-query symptom, asks a schema question → database

queries.q: what does SQL Server licensing cost for an 8-core box?
write the SQL-injection section of the onboarding security deck
queries.note: says SQL and injection, asks for a document rather than a query
